$comment: Hand-authored semantics merged by scripts/build_ontology.py. Native facts (types, fields, identity, categories, observed edges) come from the Flowsint checkout; this file adds taxonomy domains, relationship definitions, extensions, evidence and sensitivity policy. Edit here, then rebuild.

conventions.node_type_in_json: Lowercase registry key ("domain", "socialaccount"), as Flowsint stores nodeType and as native exports emit it. PascalCase class names ("Domain") are used in GraphQL and Markdown. Lookup is case-insensitive in Flowsint.
conventions.node_id: Import-local id = <key>:<canonical identity>. The identity comes from the type's identity selector and canonicalizers (identity-config-v1). Composite selectors join values with '|'. Values longer than 96 characters, values with tabs, newlines, or other control characters, and identity values of sensitivity class secret, financial, or government_id use <key>:h:<first 16 hex of sha256(canonical)>. Never reuse one id for two different entities.
conventions.node_label: The Flowsint compute_label() result. emit.py computes it with the real Pydantic model when a Flowsint interpreter is available; otherwise it falls back to the UI label_key, then the primary field.
conventions.properties: Only fields of the Flowsint type, with their declared names. Flowsint types accept extra keys (extra=allow); emit.py keeps unknown keys and reports them. Never use reserved property names.
conventions.relationship_label: UPPER_SNAKE_CASE verb phrase, read source -> target. Use a label from the relationship catalog. Prefer a native label when its definition fits. Use an extension label only when no native label fits. IS_RELATED_TO is the last resort and needs a caption that states the nature of the link.
conventions.relationship_direction: Emit one direction only. Never emit a relationship and its inverse. For symmetric labels, order the endpoints by id.
conventions.relationship_properties: Native edge properties are date, caption, type, weight, confidence_level. Put fact qualifiers (role, start_date, end_date, amount, currency) in properties as well; keep evidence in extensions.
conventions.nested_vs_edge: Flowsint types can embed other types (Whois.domain, Individual.email_addresses). When an embedded entity matters to the investigation, also emit it as its own node and connect it with the matching relationship, as the enrichers do.
conventions.one_fact_one_edge: Each relationship is one claim that can be true or false. Split compound sentences into several edges. Time-bound facts carry date or start_date/end_date.
conventions.uncertain_identity: Two mentions that may denote the same entity are two nodes linked by POSSIBLY_SAME_AS with evidence. Never merge on a guess. Merge only when the canonical identity is equal.

evidence_model.where: Node and relationship evidence lives in extensions["flowsint-ontology.evidence"] = {version: 1, data: {confidence, status, evidence: [...]}}. A short summary goes in node.metadata (extraction_id, confidence, sources) and in relationship.properties.confidence_level. The source catalog lives in the top-level extensions["flowsint-ontology.extraction"].

evidence_item.source: Id of a source in the source catalog (S1, S2, ...). Required.
evidence_item.locator: Where in the source: URL fragment, page and paragraph, line, timestamp, message id. Required when the source has more than one part.
evidence_item.quote: Verbatim excerpt that supports the claim, at most 300 characters. Redact secrets.
evidence_item.observed_at: ISO 8601 date or datetime at which the fact was true or observed, if known.

methods.stated: The source asserts the fact in words (a document, a person in a conversation, a profile field).
methods.observed: The agent or a tool saw the fact directly in technical data (DNS answer, HTTP response, file hash).
methods.inferred: The agent concluded the fact from other facts. State the reasoning in the quote or in a gap note. Cap confidence at 0.7 unless a second independent source confirms.
methods.enriched: A Flowsint enricher or an external tool produced the fact. Name the tool in locator.
methods.derived: The fact follows mechanically from another value (email domain part -> Domain, URL host -> Domain). Confidence follows the parent value.

source_reliability.A: Completely reliable: authoritative registry, official record, direct technical observation.
source_reliability.B: Usually reliable: established outlet, reputable vendor report, verified account.
source_reliability.C: Fairly reliable: generally accurate source with occasional errors.
source_reliability.D: Not usually reliable: anonymous blog, unverified account, scraped aggregator.
source_reliability.E: Unreliable: known for errors, deception, or fabrication.
source_reliability.F: Reliability cannot be judged: new or unknown source.

confirmed: Two or more independent reliable sources, or direct technical observation.
probable: One reliable source, consistent with other facts.
possible: One weak source, or an inference from reliable facts.
doubtful: Weak, contradicted, or single unreliable source.
refuted: Evidence shows the claim is false. Keep only when the refutation matters.

evidence_model.combining: Node or edge confidence = 1 - product(1 - c_i) over independent evidence items, capped at 0.99; dependent items (same origin) count once. emit.py applies this when a node or edge has no explicit confidence.

special_category.basis: GDPR art. 9 and art. 10 (racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious beliefs, health, genetic and biometric data, criminal convictions and offences).
special_category.rule: Record only when the input states it explicitly and the investigative purpose requires it. Never infer it. emit.py lists every such value in the Markdown report.

government_id.basis: National identifiers (passport, ID card, SSN, tax id, driving licence, voter id).
government_id.rule: Record only when stated in the input and required by the purpose. Never guess a format or complete a partial number.

financial.basis: Account numbers, card numbers, balances, income, credit data.
financial.rule: Record when stated and required. Keep the value exact because it is an identity field; the report masks it to the last 4 characters.

secret.basis: Live authentication material: passwords, CVV, session tokens, API keys, private keys, seed phrases.
secret.rule: Never record plaintext. Passwords: keep only a hash the source provides; never hash a plaintext password yourself (weak passwords are reversible); otherwise omit it and list it in excluded. High-entropy tokens and keys: store sha256:<hex> or a masked form (****1234). Node ids for secret identity values are hashed. emit.py blocks values that look like plaintext secrets.

domains.label: Actors
domains.definition: Persons and organisations that act, own, control, or employ; plus reified affiliations between them.

domains.label: Personas and digital identities
domains.definition: Handles, accounts, and aliases through which an actor appears online.

domains.label: Contact points and places
domains.definition: Selectors that reach or locate an actor: e-mail, phone, postal address or place.

domains.label: Internet infrastructure
domains.definition: Naming, addressing, routing, and registration of internet resources.

domains.label: Web presence
domains.definition: Websites and what they run or embed.

domains.label: Access and threat
domains.definition: Authentication material, devices, sessions, malicious software, and exposure events.

domains.label: Content and artefacts
domains.definition: Documents, files, messages, and free text that carry or mention facts.

domains.label: Financial instruments and value transfer
domains.definition: Accounts, cards, wallets, transactions, and tokens.

domains.label: Analytic assessments
domains.definition: Scores and profiles that evaluate another entity. They are judgements, not observations.

Individual.identity_tip: full_name is the identity; set it even when only first_name/last_name are known ("Jane Doe").
Individual.avoid: Do not create an Individual from a bare handle; use Username.

Organization.recognize: Company, agency, NGO, group, party, criminal organisation.
Organization.identity_tip: name as written in the most authoritative source; put legal identifiers (siren, ...) in properties.
Organization.avoid: Do not use Organization for a brand of software (Technology) or a website (Website).

Affiliation.recognize: A role of a person in an organisation that needs its own dates, department, or source.
Affiliation.identity_tip: organization is the identity; prefer a WORKS_FOR / MEMBER_OF edge with role and dates unless the affiliation must carry its own evidence trail.
Affiliation.avoid: Do not duplicate a WORKS_FOR edge with an Affiliation node for the same fact.

Username.recognize: A handle without a confirmed platform account ("@jdoe", "jdoe92").
Username.identity_tip: value without the leading @; platform as property.
Username.avoid: When the platform and profile are known, also create SocialAccount and link Username -HAS_SOCIAL_ACCOUNT-> SocialAccount.

SocialAccount.recognize: A concrete account on a platform (profile URL, platform + handle).
SocialAccount.identity_tip: identity = platform + username.value; always set both.
SocialAccount.avoid: Do not put the profile URL only in Website.

Alias.recognize: Another name an actor uses: nickname, nom de guerre, trade name.
Alias.avoid: A handle on a platform is a Username, not an Alias.

Gravatar.recognize: Gravatar profile tied to an e-mail hash.

Email.identity_tip: preserve local-part case; domain lowercased IDNA.
Email.avoid: Obfuscated forms ("jdoe [at] example [dot] com") must be de-obfuscated, with method=derived.

Phone.identity_tip: E.164 (+34600000000). A national number without a known region cannot be canonicalised: keep the raw text in Phrase and add a gap.
Phone.avoid: Do not guess the country code.

Location.identity_tip: address, city, country, and zip are all required by the type; use "unknown" only when the source lacks the part and say so in a gap.

Domain.identity_tip: lowercase IDNA A-label, no trailing dot; root=true for the registrable domain.
Domain.avoid: A URL is a Website; derive its Domain with BELONGS_TO_DOMAIN.

Ip.avoid: Defanged forms (1.2.3[.]4) are re-fanged with method=derived.

CIDR.identity_tip: network address with host bits masked.

Port.recognize: Open or observed TCP/UDP port on a host.
Port.identity_tip: number; identity is the number alone, so always connect it to its Ip with HAS_PORT.

Whois.recognize: A WHOIS registration record of a domain.

Website.identity_tip: absolute URL with scheme; default port removed.
Website.avoid: Do not use Website for a bare domain.

WebTracker.recognize: Analytics/ad tracker id (UA-, G-, GTM-, pixel id).

Technology.recognize: Software, framework, or product a site or host uses.

Script.recognize: A script file or snippet (JS, PowerShell, bash).

Credential.recognize: Login material tied to a service.
Credential.identity_tip: username; service = the system it logs into (domain or app), omitted when unknown. The leak it came from is a Leak node via FOUND_IN_LEAK.
Credential.avoid: Never store a plaintext password and never hash one yourself; keep password_hash only when the source gives a hash.

Session.recognize: An authenticated session or session token.
Session.identity_tip: session_id is a secret: store sha256:<hex>.

Device.recognize: Phone, computer, IoT device, or browser fingerprint.
Device.identity_tip: device_id (IMEI, serial, hardware id, stealer-log machine id).

Malware.identity_tip: name; family as property; sample hashes in sample_hashes or as File nodes.

Leak.recognize: A leak or dump that is not a catalogued breach (paste, combolist, internal leak).

Document.recognize: A document with title (report, PDF, contract, article).
Document.identity_tip: title; hashes and source_url in properties.
Document.avoid: The analysed input itself becomes a Document node only when it matters to the investigation.

File.recognize: A file seen on disk or in transit.

Message.recognize: An e-mail, chat, SMS, or post with sender/recipients.
Message.identity_tip: message_id; when the source has none, derive it as <platform>:<sender>:<timestamp>.

Phrase.recognize: Free text worth keeping that fits no other type (slogan, keyword, unparsed selector).
Phrase.avoid: Phrase is the fallback type, not a dumping ground; prefer a precise type.

BankAccount.identity_tip: account_number exactly as written (no separator removal).

CryptoWallet.identity_tip: lowercase Ethereum (0x...) only; keep the case of other chains.

CryptoWalletTransaction.identity_tip: hash (lowercase); source wallet is required by the type.

CryptoNFT.identity_tip: contract_address + token_id; wallet required by the type.

RiskProfile.recognize: A risk assessment of another entity.
RiskProfile.identity_tip: entity_id = id of the assessed node.

ReputationScore.recognize: A provider's reputation score for another entity.
ReputationScore.identity_tip: entity_id = id of the scored node.

IS_{contact_type}_CONTACT.reason: contact_type iterates WHOIS contact roles registrant, administrative, technical, billing (uppercased).

IS_{contact_type.upper()}_CONTACT.reason: contact_type iterates WHOIS contact roles registrant, administrative, technical, billing.

IS_RELATED_T0.reason: Upstream typo (digit zero) in the test-only domain_to_dummy enricher.

RELATED_TO.reason: Default of the embedded agent graph.relations.create tool (domain_tools.py); the UI, enricher base, and importers default to IS_RELATED_TO.

flowsint-enrichers/src/flowsint_enricher.note: item is Domain or Email (dummy data).

flowsint-enrichers/src/flowsint_enricher.anomaly: Upstream emits Individual -WORKS_FOR-> Email. Semantically wrong: use Individual -HAS_EMAIL-> Email.

IS_RELATED_TO.definition: Generic link whose nature no catalogued label expresses. Flowsint default label.
IS_RELATED_TO.notes: Last resort. Requires a caption that states the nature of the link; emit.py rejects it without one.

WORKS_FOR.definition: The person is employed by, or works on behalf of, the target (organisation, or the person that WHOIS lists as the main contact).

HAS_LEADER.definition: The organisation has the person as director, officer, executive, or legal representative.

MEMBER_OF.definition: The actor belongs to a group, association, party, board, or network, without an employment relation.

SUBSIDIARY_OF.definition: The organisation is owned or controlled by the target organisation (subsidiary, branch, front).

HAS_AFFILIATION.definition: The person holds the reified Affiliation (role with its own dates and evidence).

AFFILIATION_WITH.definition: The reified Affiliation is with the target organisation.

RELATIVE_OF.definition: The persons are family members. Put the kind of kinship in properties.type (spouse, parent, sibling, child, ...); for directed kinship order source as the elder or the parent.

ASSOCIATE_OF.definition: The actors have a social or business association that no more precise label covers (partner, co-founder, co-defendant, frequent contact).

OWNS.definition: The source legally or beneficially owns the target. Native use: wallet owns NFT.
OWNS.notes: For operational control without proven ownership use CONTROLS.

CONTROLS.definition: The actor operates or administers the target without proven ownership (account operator, infrastructure administrator, nominee arrangement).

HAS_ALIAS.definition: The source is also known by the alias.

POSSIBLY_SAME_AS.definition: Identity hypothesis: the two nodes may denote the same real-world entity. Both nodes stay separate until a human decides.
POSSIBLY_SAME_AS.notes: Both endpoints must have the same type. confidence_level states the strength of the hypothesis; evidence states the matching features.

HAS_USERNAME.definition: The source uses or exposes the handle. Native use: the local part of an e-mail as a candidate handle.

HAS_SOCIAL_ACCOUNT.definition: The handle (or actor) has the account on a platform.

HAS_GRAVATAR.definition: The e-mail address has the Gravatar profile.

CONNECTION_WITH.definition: A breach or intelligence record links the selector to the person. Weak association, not proof of ownership.
CONNECTION_WITH.notes: Native in the dehashed and intelligence enrichers. Prefer HAS_EMAIL / HAS_PHONE / HAS_USERNAME (person as source) when a source states that the person uses the selector.

HAS_EMAIL.definition: The source uses, publishes, or is reachable at the e-mail address.

HAS_PHONE.definition: The source uses, publishes, or is reachable at the phone number.

LIVES_AT.definition: The person resides or resided at the place.

HAS_ADDRESS.definition: The organisation's registered or head-office address.

LOCATED_AT.definition: The source is physically at the place (establishment, server geolocation, device position, item found). Native use: organisation establishment.
LOCATED_AT.notes: For a person, use LIVES_AT for residence and LOCATED_AT with a date for presence at a time.

REGISTERED_IN.definition: The domain's registrant is located at the place, according to WHOIS.

RESOLVES_TO.definition: DNS A/AAAA resolution of the domain returns the IP.

REVERSE_RESOLVES_TO.definition: The IP's PTR record names the domain.
REVERSE_RESOLVES_TO.notes: Not a strict inverse of RESOLVES_TO: PTR and A records are independent. Emit the one actually observed.

HOSTS.definition: The IP serves the domain or website (passive DNS, reverse-IP, virtual hosting).

HAS_SUBDOMAIN.definition: The parent domain has the child hostname.

HAS_RELATED_DOMAIN.definition: The domains share registrant data or history (reverse WHOIS, historical records).
HAS_RELATED_DOMAIN.notes: Direction from the investigated domain to the discovered domain.

HAS_WHOIS.definition: The domain has the WHOIS registration record.

REGISTERED_BY.definition: The WHOIS record names the target as registrant contact.

HAS_DOMAIN.definition: The source is bound to the domain: registrant organisation, e-mail domain part, or website host.

HAS_REGISTERED_DOMAIN.definition: The actor or e-mail appears as registrant of the domain (reverse WHOIS).

IS_REGISTRANT_CONTACT.definition: The actor is the registrant contact of the domain in WHOIS.

IS_ADMINISTRATIVE_CONTACT.definition: The actor is the administrative contact of the domain in WHOIS.

IS_TECHNICAL_CONTACT.definition: The actor is the technical contact of the domain in WHOIS.

IS_BILLING_CONTACT.definition: The actor is the billing contact of the domain in WHOIS.

HOSTED_IN.definition: The domain's addresses are announced by the autonomous system.

BELONGS_TO.definition: The IP, prefix, or organisation belongs to the autonomous system (routing or operator relation).

ANNOUNCES.definition: The autonomous system originates the IP prefix in BGP.

CONTAINS.definition: The source contains the target: prefix contains address or sub-prefix; archive or document contains a file. Native use: CIDR contains IP.

HAS_PORT.definition: The IP exposes the port (open, filtered, or observed).

HAS_DNS_RECORD.definition: The domain has the DNS resource record.

POINTS_TO.definition: The DNS record's value designates the target (A/AAAA -> Ip; CNAME/NS/MX/PTR -> Domain).

HAS_CERTIFICATE.definition: The host presents the X.509 certificate.

CERTIFICATE_COVERS.definition: The certificate names the domain in its subject CN or SAN.

ISSUED_BY.definition: The certificate or card was issued by the organisation (CA, card issuer).

TLS_INFO.definition: A TLS handshake on the domain produced the HTTPS website node that carries the certificate details (domain_to_tls).
TLS_INFO.notes: Native only. For new certificate facts use HAS_CERTIFICATE -> SSLCertificate.

BELONGS_TO_DOMAIN.definition: The website's host is the domain.

LINKS_TO.definition: The source contains a hyperlink to the target.

IS_SUBDOMAIN.definition: Native direction (website_to_subdomains): the parent website -> a website served on one of its subdomains.
IS_SUBDOMAIN.notes: The label reads backwards; keep the native direction. For Domain -> Domain use HAS_SUBDOMAIN.

USES_TECHNOLOGY.definition: The website or host runs the technology.

HAS_TRACKER.definition: The website embeds the tracker id.

HAS_INNER_TEXT.definition: The website's visible text contains the phrase.

HAS_SCRIPT.definition: The website loads or embeds the script.

HAS_CREDENTIAL.definition: The selector or actor has the login credential.

HAS_SESSION.definition: The credential or account opened the session.

ORIGINATED_FROM.definition: The session, message, or connection came from the IP or device.

ASSOCIATED_WITH_DEVICE.definition: The selector was found on, or used from, the device (infostealer logs). Native use: e-mail, phone, username.

FOUND_IN_BREACH.definition: The selector appears in the catalogued breach.

FOUND_IN_LEAK.definition: The selector or artefact appears in the leak or dump.

USES_MALWARE.definition: The actor deploys or operates the malware.

COMMUNICATES_WITH.definition: The malware, device, or host makes network contact with the target (C2, beacon, exfiltration endpoint).

DROPS.definition: The malware or script writes or downloads the file, script, or second-stage malware.

SAMPLE_OF.definition: The file or script is a sample of the malware family.

DISTRIBUTED_VIA.definition: The malware or file is distributed through the website, domain, message, or account.

SENT.definition: The sender (account, address, number, or actor) sent the message.

SENT_TO.definition: The message was addressed to the recipient.
SENT_TO.notes: properties.type = to | cc | bcc | dm | group.

REPLY_TO.definition: The message replies to the earlier message.

HAS_ATTACHMENT.definition: The message carries the file or document.

AUTHORED.definition: The actor or account wrote or created the content.

PUBLISHED_ON.definition: The content was published at the website or account.

MENTIONS.definition: The content names or refers to the entity without asserting a stronger relation.
MENTIONS.notes: Use it to link a relevant source document to the entities it reports; use the specific label for the fact itself.

TRANSACTION.definition: On-chain transfer from the source wallet to the target wallet. Native: created by cryptowallet_to_transactions via create_wallet_transactions, merged on hash.
TRANSACTION.notes: Put the transaction hash in properties.hash: Flowsint merges TRANSACTION edges on it.

SENT_TRANSACTION.definition: The wallet is the sender of the reified transaction node.

TRANSACTION_TO.definition: The reified transaction pays the target wallet.

TRANSFERRED_TO.definition: Off-chain value transfer (wire, card payment, cash) from the source to the target.
TRANSFERRED_TO.notes: For on-chain transfers between wallets use the native TRANSACTION.

HELD_AT.definition: The account or card is held at the financial institution.

HAS_RISK_PROFILE.definition: The entity is assessed by the risk profile. Native use: IP fraud score.

HAS_REPUTATION.definition: The entity has the reputation score from a provider.
